text:
maya: Quick heads up — p50 for FP8 continuous rollout jumped ~18% in prod-us-west after yesterday's kernel-selector change. Model: gpt-xxl-8k, typical seq=1024 slices.
lee: ugh, saw the alert. Is this across all instance types or GPU-specific?
maya: Mostly T4p/c6-like infra. Profiling shows kernel choice flipping from the FP8 fused matmul (fast path) to an INT8 fallback with extra re-quant ops for certain batch shapes.
arpit: Can you paste the perf counters? L2 miss / stall numbers?
maya: Sure — snip from perf dump (30s window):
```
requests: 4k
avg_batch_size: 7.2
p50_latency: 132ms (prev 112ms)
throughput_tokens/s: -12%
kernel_path_changes: 23% of calls selected fallback
L2_misses/sec: 1.8M (up 45%)
warp_serialize_count: +32%
kv_cache_evictions: +6% (micro-slab misalignment)
```
noah: The "kernel_path_changes" jumps ring a bell — we added an extra shape-safety guard in selector v2.3 to avoid numerical edge cases with FP8. That guard rehydrates tensors to int8 in some narrow skyline shapes.
sara: Could be the padding pattern from continuous batching — pad-to-row is causing a few big rows that trip the guard. Our histograms show a new spike at width=2048 after the batcher change.
lee: If padding causes wide rows, kernel selector might choose kernels with different tiling that touch KV layout. That could cause extra cache-line churn and kv_cache_evictions.
maya: I ran a targeted repro on staging. With pad_strategy=pad-to-row we see the fallback; with pad_strategy=pad-to-min (pack tighter) the FP8 path stays. Numbers: p50 110ms vs 131ms.
arpit: So two interacting issues: (1) selector guard conservative for some shapes, (2) continuous batcher padding creating those shapes more often.
noah: Agreed. Also saw microbatch spill: when avg_batch_size ~7 we occasionally hit the threshold that forces allocation on device that hits a different allocator path -> worse alignment -> kv slab split.
sara: Can we relax the guard to check quantization calibration score instead of shape-only? We have calibration stats per model variant in Optimize. If calibration_confidence>0.92, allow FP8 even for those shapes.
lee: That seems reasonable. Alternatively, add a pad-aware hint to selector: expose "expected_row_padding" metric from batcher so selector can make an informed decision.
maya: I prototyped the calibration gate locally — gating on calibration_confidence prevented the fallback and kept p50 stable. But we need a safety net: if output kl-divergence > threshold, revert.
arpit: Also want to avoid a case where a small portion of requests still choose fallback and cause perf jitter. Maybe we should A/B the selector change with a sticky session so a thread stays on one kernel selection for its whole lifetime.
noah: Good call. Sticky kernel per request (or per KV session) would reduce mid-sequence kernel switching that invalidates KV cache.
sara: Action plan suggestion: 1) revert conservative shape guard in selector -> roll forward calibration-gate 2) add pad-hint telemetry from batcher 3) add sticky kernel hint to routing 4) run 24h canary on us-west low-traffic pool.
maya: I'll open an RFC and a short PR with the calibration-gate. Will include perf smoke: p50/p95 and kv_eviction counter baseline + after.
lee: I can wire pad-hint telemetry into the batcher this afternoon. It's a small change: add expected_padding_ratio field to BatchSummary emitted to trace.
arpit: I'll sketch the sticky-kernel proposal in the scheduler — simplest is a per-request token that pins kernel choice for the request id. We can make it opt-in.
infra-bot: deploy-bot noticed a test failure in selector v2.3 on linux-xla-test-03. Job: selector-integration-tests. Failure: quant-sanity-check flake.
maya: @lee @arpit fyi infra-bot flagged the test. Might be related to the earlier guard — good to fix before wide rollout.
noah: TL;DR — regression caused by interaction: padding pattern from continuous batching -> shapes that trip selector guard -> fallback to slower path -> KV slab misalignment + cache evictions -> higher latency. Fix: calibration gate + pad telemetry + sticky kernel + canary.
sara: I'll add an eval check for model variants so calibration gating has an automated rollback if quality degrades.
maya: Thanks team. I'll post the RFC and link the PR when ready. Leaving a checklist in-thread: 
- [ ] RFC + design (maya)
- [ ] PR for calibration-gate (maya)
- [ ] pad-hint telemetry (lee)
- [ ] sticky-kernel opt-in (arpit)
- [ ] 24h canary (ops)
- [ ] roll monitor dashboards (sara)

maya: ping me for pairing on the PR review. :thumbsup:
